ITC stock plans to absorb Yoga Bar maker after board approval
sum: ITC's board approved a scheme on November 2, 2026, to merge wholly owned Sproutlife Foods Private Limited into the parent company. ET Retail reported that the scheme is subject to statutory and regulatory approvals and is intended to take effect from April 1, 2026.

Sproutlife makes bars, muesli, oats, protein-rich foods and peanut butter under the digital-first Yoga Bar brand. It reported turnover of INR 451.71 crore, total assets of INR 150.07 crore and net worth of INR 5.22 crore in fiscal 2026, based on audited standalone accounts.

ITC said the merger should integrate operations, improve the use of financial and managerial resources and simplify the group structure by reducing the number of operating entities. Because Sproutlife is wholly owned, its shares held by ITC and its nominees will be cancelled when the scheme becomes effective. ITC will issue no new shares, and the shareholding pattern will not change.

The transaction comes after ITC's September-quarter results. ET Retail reported an 18.5 percent decline in consolidated net profit to INR 4,229 crore, while net revenue rose 5 percent to INR 20,454 crore. Weaker cigarette earnings weighed on profitability, although the FMCG, agriculture and paper businesses delivered stronger growth.

For investors, the merger is primarily a structural step rather than an immediate share issuance or ownership event. The key next milestones are the required approvals and the execution of the scheme, alongside progress in ITC's non-cigarette businesses.
Investors can place ITC's corporate developments alongside the BSE Sensex market environment.

sum: Muhurat trading will take place on Diwali (Sunday, November 8) between 2:20 PM and 3:50 PM (pre-open session to closing session). Jainam, an end to end financial services company, has released its annual Diwali Muhurat Picks 2026, which identifies five stocks for the year ahead. Jainam has recommended Target price and stop loss levels too.

Diwali Muhurat Picks 2026: Over the Samvat 2082 period, equity market performance varied across market-cap segments, with the Nifty 50 declining 10.88% and the Sensex falling 11.81% between the Muhurat Trading session on October 21, 2025, and October 30, 2026, Jainam pointed out. The Nifty Midcap 150 and Nifty Smallcap index declined 4.21% and 3.02%, respectively. The report examines these movements alongside evolving valuations, domestic investment activity and the global developments influencing Indian capital markets. For Samvat 2083, Jainam’s research team has identified five stocks through a combination of fundamental and technical analysis: The Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL), HDFC Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Tech Mahindra and Bharti Hexacom. Let’s have a look at these stocks.

It is India’s largest hotel company with 390 operating hotels and 280 more in the pipeline across Taj, Vivanta, Ginger and other brands. Growth is accelerating: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22% with occupancy at 82%, and the management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 15-17%. 94% of the pipeline is asset-light, management fees grew 25% in Q2, and the company holds about 1,500 cr of net cash with AAA ratings from ICRA and CARE. Key risks are a rich valuation (54.4x trailing P/E), West Asia disruption and a 11,874 or rent claim on the Taj Mahal Palace.

It is India’s largest private bank, with about 14% of all bank loans, trades near decade-low valuations at 1.9x book and 14x earnings after a 30% fall in a year, even as FY26 profit grew 10.9%. Growth is back, with Q2 FY27 loans up 16.3% and deposits up 18.8%, largely closing the post-merger funding gap. About 70% of loans are floating-rate and should reprice upward after the RBI hike, while asset quality stays pristine (gross NPA 1.11%, CET1 17.1%). Key risks are the leadership transition, NIM slipping to 3.16% and continued Fll selling.

Digital brands, premium FMCG to drive ITC's growth ambitions
sum: Amid challenges in its cigarettes business, ITC is focusing on expanding its non-cigarette offerings. The FMCG segment has shown significant growth, leading to an improved product mix and margins. Digital-first brands such as Yoga Bar and Prasuma have also reported strong revenue increases. The paperboard and agri businesses are benefiting from rising demand and exports of value-added products.
After remaining range-bound for the past three months, the stock has gained 5.1% in two trading sessions since the company reported its September-quarter results on Monday evening.
Read more: Lenskart Q2 Results: Profit zooms 122% YoY to Rs 227 crore; revenue grows 36%

The FMCG business continued to emerge as a key growth driver, with the FMCG-others segment delivering its highest growth in 14 quarters, led by strong demand across foods, biscuits, snacks, dairy, personal care, notebooks and home-care categories. The segment's margin expanded by more than 50 basis points year-on-year and on a sequential basis, despite inflationary pressures, supported by an improved product mix, cost-management initiatives and calibrated pricing actions.

Meanwhile, digital-first brands such as Yoga Bar, Prasuma and Mother Sparsh maintained strong momentum, posting 70% year-on-year growth and crossing a combined annual revenue run rate of more than ₹1,800 crore.
Read more: Dabur India Q2 Results: Profit rises 12% YoY to Rs 506 crore, revenue up 12%; co declares interim dividend of Rs 3.50/share

The paper business also maintained strong momentum, driven by improved demand and the integration of Century Pulp & Paper, while the agri business continued to benefit from growth in value-added products and exports.

ITC shares surge 9% in five sessions: What is fuelling the rally in the cigarette major?
sum: Shares of ITC extended their winning streak on Wednesday, gaining over 9% in five trading sessions amid value buying following the September-quarter earnings announcement. The rally comes despite the cigarette-to-FMCG conglomerate reporting a weak set of Q2 FY27 results, with consolidated profit declining nearly 19% year-on-year and EBITDA margins contracting sharply.

On Wednesday, ITC shares surged as much as 3.7% to an intraday high of ₹283.50 on the BSE, taking its market capitalisation to around ₹3.51 lakh crore. The stock has gained around 6% since the company announced its Q2 FY27 results after market hours on Monday.

The FMCG heavyweight has gained nearly 12% from its 52-week low of ₹252.80, touched during intraday trade on October 28, 2026. Despite the recent recovery, the FMCG stock remains down nearly 32% from its 52-week high of ₹414.65, recorded on November 4, 2025.
Technically, the stock has moved above its five-day, 20-day, 50-day and 100-day moving averages, although it continues to trade below its 200-day moving average.

For September quarter of FY27, ITC reported consolidated profit at ₹4,168.40 crore, compared with ₹5,126.11 crore a year ago. Consolidated EBITDA fell 15.7% to ₹5,644.83 crore, while EBITDA margin contracted sharply to 27.9% from 34.3%, reflecting pressure on operating profitability.

Revenue from operations, however, rose 43.9% to ₹30,578.40 crore, largely due to higher excise duty on cigarettes. Excluding excise duty, revenue grew by 3.9% to ₹20,268.63 crore from ₹19,501.63 crore in the year-ago quarter.
One of the key factors supporting sentiment is the expected gradual recovery in the profitability of ITC's cigarette business, which remains a significant contributor to the company's earnings.

sum: - ITC Limited reported Q2 net profit of ₹4,137 crore, down 20%.
- ITC Limited's Q2 revenue increased 44%, although the absolute revenue figure was not disclosed in the source.
- ITC acquired the remaining 52.5% of Sproutlife Foods for about ₹645 crore on September 28, 2026.
- ITC's board approved Sproutlife's proposed amalgamation on November 2, 2026, subject to approvals.
ITC reported net profit of ₹4,137 crore for the quarter, representing a 20% year-on-year decline. Revenue, however, rose 44%, showing a sharp increase in the company’s top line during the period.

The company said cigarette earnings fell, while its other FMCG business grew. The reported performance therefore reflected differing trends across ITC’s businesses, with growth in non-cigarette consumer categories occurring alongside a decline in cigarette segment earnings.

ITC also stated that its other FMCG segment included Sproutlife Foods from April 1, 2026. As a result, the company said the segment’s figures are not comparable with earlier periods. This disclosure is important when assessing growth in the FMCG business because the consolidation changes the reporting base.

sum: Stocks to buy | Ganesh Dongre's stock recommendations today: The key benchmark indices of the Indian stock market ended the week on a positive note, with the Nifty 50 index gaining nearly 0.44% to close at 22,520, while the Bank Nifty advanced 1.48% to settle at 55,256. Sectoral performance was broadly positive, with most major sectors recording gains in the range of 1–6% during the week. However, the overall market sentiment remains cautious amid elevated geopolitical uncertainties, particularly ongoing US–Iran tensions and broader developments in the Middle East. Rising crude oil prices and higher global bond yields continue to pose challenges for global trade, inflation expectations and overall investor sentiment.

As highlighted in our previous weekly outlook, the Nifty has entered oversold territory following the recent sharp correction. The decline has been driven by a combination of global risk-off sentiment and concerns surrounding the US Federal Reserve’s interest-rate outlook. The possibility of further interest-rate hikes by the Fed and the RBI in the coming quarters remains a key concern for equity markets. Additionally, the upward bias in US 10-year Treasury yields could continue to influence global risk appetite and foreign institutional investor (FII) flows into emerging markets, including India.

Ganesh Dongre, AVP — Equity Research at Anand Rathi, believes the Nifty 50 index faced strong resistance in the 24,500–24,600 zone last month, which also coincided with the broader 200-day EMA resistance area. Subsequently, the index witnessed a sharp decline towards the 22,500–22,000 zone, approaching the lows recorded in March 2026 and a significant support region based on the previous six-month price structure.

“A sustained weekly close above 23,200 would help improve the near-term technical outlook and could open the door for a recovery towards 24,000–24,200, where the 200-day EMA and broader resistance levels are positioned. On the downside, 22,000–21,700 remains a crucial support zone, as it represents a significant historical support area near previous yearly and quarterly lows,” Ganesh Dongre of Anand Ratahi said.

sum: ITC shares fell nearly 4 per cent on Thursday, making it the top loser on the Nifty 50, after a large block deal worth ₹9,437 crore changed hands in the pre-open session. The stock was trading at ₹255.25 on the NSE at 11.26 am, down ₹10.45 or 3.93 per cent, hovering just above its 52-week low of ₹254.65 hit on October 1.

As many as 36.66 crore ITC shares, representing approximately 2.9 per cent of the company’s outstanding equity, were traded in the block deal window at an average price of ₹257 per share. The identities of the buyers and sellers were not immediately disclosed.

The transaction follows a disclosure earlier this week that US-based fund house GQG Partners LLC had sold 3.97 crore ITC shares through on-market transactions between May 28, 2025, and October 5, 2026. The combined shareholding of GQG Partners and its persons acting in concert fell to 3.17 per cent from 3.48 per cent of ITC’s total voting capital.

ITC has lost 29.89 per cent year-to-date, significantly underperforming the Nifty 50, which is down 14.45 per cent over the same period. The stock’s 52-week high stands at ₹426.40, touched on October 31, 2025, reflecting a drawdown of roughly 40 per cent from that peak. The company’s total market capitalisation stood at ₹3,19,716 crore as of Thursday morning, with total traded volume of 283.77 lakh shares worth ₹735.05 crore by mid-session.

ITC has no promoter shareholding. Among its major institutional investors, the Specified Undertaking of the Unit Trust of India held 7.78 per cent as of June 30, while Life Insurance Corporation of India and domestic mutual funds held 16.3 per cent and 16.5 per cent, respectively.

The stock is also navigating headwinds in its core cigarettes business following a 40 per cent GST rate on tobacco products effective February 1, which prompted multiple rounds of price increases. The Classic Connect 20-cigarette pack now retails at ₹428, up from ₹300 at the start of the year, while the Gold Flake Super Star 10-pack has risen to ₹89 from ₹59 over the same period. sum: ITC share price: Shares of ITC gained nearly 3 per cent in Monday’s intraday trade after global brokerage Citi upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Sell’ and raised its target price to Rs 300. The brokerage sees nearly 17 per cent upside from the stock’s previous close of Rs 257.

The upgrade came despite near-term pressure on ITC’s cigarette business following the sharp increase in cigarette taxation. Citi said the recent correction in the stock has factored in risks related to volumes and profitability, making the current risk-reward more favourable.

On the BSE, ITC shares climbed as much as 2.8 per cent to Rs 264.25 during the session. At 13:48 pm, the stock was trading 2.33 per cent higher at Rs 261.85, while the benchmark Sensex was up 0.53 per cent at 72,287. Around 32.4 million ITC shares had changed hands across the exchanges.

Citi expects cigarette EBIT to decline 23 per cent in FY27, citing the impact of higher taxation as well as competition from branded and illicit products. However, the brokerage believes the earnings downgrade cycle is now largely over.

According to Citi, ITC has already taken steps to offset the impact of higher taxes through calibrated price increases and portfolio interventions. Around 75 per cent of the tax increase has, as per Citi’s estimates, already been passed on through price hikes.
The brokerage expects new launches in the LSFT and Premium-DSFT categories to help retain consumers within ITC’s portfolio and limit downtrading.

sum: As per a stock exchange filing, ITC Infotech will first acquire a 22.1% stake in Happiest Minds from founder and promoter Ashok Soota for Rs 1,330 crore, with the purchase split across two tranches. The initial transaction will then be followed by a share swap between the two companies, under which shareholders will receive 25 ITC Infotech shares for every 81 Happiest Minds shares held.

Following the completion of the merger, ITC Infotech will be listed on the stock exchanges through a backdoor listing. ITC Ltd will hold a 73.4% stake in the merged entity, while Soota and his promoter entities will own 7.6%. Public shareholders will hold the remaining 19%.

Happiest Minds has been assigned an equity value of Rs 6,167 crore for the transaction, while ITC Infotech has been valued at Rs 11,920 crore. Together, the two companies have a combined valuation of more than Rs 18,000 crore.

Ashok Soota, who founded Happiest Minds in 2011, said he was delighted that, after the completion of the legal formalities, the company would become an important part of a larger organisation through its amalgamation with ITC Infotech. He said the two organisations were aligned in their values and shared vision for the future, while their business portfolios had significant complementarity that would ensure synergies.
The company said the transaction would make the merged entity India's 11th-largest IT services company, with aggregate annual revenue of Rs 7,033 crore in fiscal 2026.

ITC Infotech Reportedly Eyes 44% Stake in Happiest Minds
sum: ITC Infotech is reportedly moving closer to acquiring a controlling stake of around 44% in Bengaluru-based Happiest Minds Technologies from founder Ashok Soota and promoter entities, in what could become one of the bigger consolidation moves in India's mid-tier IT services market.
Multiple media reports have placed the potential transaction value at around ₹2,800 crore to ₹2,900 crore. Neither ITC Infotech nor Happiest Minds has formally announced a transaction so far.

Earlier reports had suggested a possible two-part structure, with ITC Infotech directly acquiring around 22% of Happiest Minds from the promoters and the remaining promoter holding potentially being part of a separate share-based transaction. A price range of around ₹390–₹400 per share was reported for the direct purchase component.
The final transaction structure, pricing and timelines have not been officially disclosed.
Founded by IT industry veteran Ashok Soota in 2011, Happiest Minds has built its business around digital engineering and newer enterprise technologies.

The company today describes itself as an AI-first digital engineering player, with capabilities spanning product and digital engineering, GenAI, cybersecurity, analytics, cloud and infrastructure management, automation and the Internet of Things.

That portfolio makes the reported transaction strategically relevant for ITC Infotech as enterprise technology spending shifts increasingly toward AI-led transformation, cloud modernization, data platforms and engineering services.

sum: ITC might need to hike prices by “at least 15%” to pass on the overall impact to consumers, if not higher. ITC gets over 40% of its revenue from cigarettes.
Shares of India's largest cigarette maker ITC Ltd. fell the most in six years after the government imposed higher tax on tobacco products.

From 1 February 2026, cigarettes will be charged an excise duty of ₹2,050-8,500 per 1,000 sticks, according to a government notification released late Wednesday. That's on top of GST at 40% on tobacco-based products and cigarettes—also kicking in from 1 February.

ITC's share price dropped as much as 9.8%, the most since 2020, while Godfrey Phillips India Ltd. dropped 17.6% on the BSE. ITC sells cigarette brands like Classic and Gold Flake, while Godfrey sells Marlboro and Four Square.

On 22 September 2025, the Narendra Modi government cut GST rates on soaps to small cars in the biggest indirect tax reforms since goods and services tax first came into effect on 1 July 2017. The rationalisation reduced the number of GST slabs to two (5% and 18%) from four (5%, 12%, 18% and 28%). A new GST slab of 40% was introduced for so-called sin goods—tobacco products and luxury items such as SUVs to Swiss watches and handbags.

The GST compensation cess was scrapped as part of the overhaul, which would have reduced the effective tax rate on tobacco products, but now an even higher excise duty has replaced it. The taxation is expected to make up the shortfall in GST revenue from other product categories.
At 25.3 crore people, India has the second-highest population of tobacco users.
